what_happens: Teachers raise a glowing dome over Hogwarts and animate stone knights to defend it; Voldemort's army pounds the shield with curses until it shatters, and Death Eaters, giants and spiders storm the castle.
why: Yates builds the siege from a wide, painterly shot of the shield taking hits, intercut with students watching from the walls, then breaks into fragmented ground-level chaos as the franchise's home becomes a war zone.

film: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
scene: First task: the Hungarian Horntail
query: Harry Potter Goblet of Fire Hungarian Horntail dragon task scene
what_happens: In the Triwizard Tournament's first task, Harry summons his broom to escape a Hungarian Horntail; the dragon breaks its chain and chases him across the castle's towers and rooftops.
why: Newell expands the book's arena task into an aerial chase, flying a CG dragon and a swooping virtual camera around Hogwarts' towers, so the spectacle becomes a pursuit with shifting geography rather than a static bout.

scene: Opening: the cottage attack and Don's escape
query: 28 Weeks Later opening scene cottage
what_happens: Infected burst into an isolated country cottage where survivors are hiding; Don abandons his wife at a window and flees across open fields, pursued by a sprinting horde, until he reaches a boat on the river.
why: Fresnadillo uses frantic handheld camera, smeared shutter effects and John Murphy's pounding score to make the run feel endless, and the moral shock of Don's choice drives the entire film.
period: English countryside, during the Rage virus outbreak

scene: The crawlers emerge
query: The Descent crawler first appearance scene
what_happens: Deep in an uncharted cave, the women glimpse a pale, eyeless humanoid through a camcorder's night-vision screen, and moments later the crawlers swarm out of the darkness.
why: Marshall lights the caves only with flares, head torches and night vision, so the audience sees exactly what the characters see; the shift from red flare to green camcorder view turns lighting into the scare mechanism.
period: Uncharted cave system, Appalachian Mountains, mid-2000s

scene: Opening: the tornado that kills Kate's team
query: Twisters 2024 opening tornado scene
what_happens: Kate's college storm-chasing crew tries to tame an Oklahoma tornado with chemical canisters, but the twister explodes into a monster that kills most of her friends, including her boyfriend.
why: Shot on 35mm under real Oklahoma skies, the prologue grounds its digital tornado in physical wind, debris and pelting rain, and uses sound design to make the storm feel like a living predator.
period: Rural Oklahoma, five years before the main story

scene: Tornadoes tear through Los Angeles
query: The Day After Tomorrow Los Angeles tornado scene
what_happens: A swarm of tornadoes descends on Los Angeles, shredding the Hollywood sign and the Capitol Records tower and hurling cars and debris through the streets as news crews broadcast the destruction live.
why: Emmerich builds the sequence from news-helicopter and street-level viewpoints, making a fully digital disaster feel like live coverage, and lets famous landmarks being destroyed communicate scale instantly.
period: Los Angeles during an abrupt climate shift, mid-2000s

scene: Yellowstone supervolcano eruption
query: 2012 Yellowstone eruption scene
what_happens: Jackson grabs a conspiracy broadcaster's map as Yellowstone's caldera explodes, then races back through raining fireballs and a vast ash cloud to escape by plane.
why: Emmerich escalates in clear stages, from tremors to the bulging dome to the blast, and keeps a tiny vehicle in frame against the expanding cloud so the impossible scale stays legible; Harrelson's gleeful broadcaster adds dark comedy.

scene: Tsunami over the Golden Gate Bridge
query: San Andreas tsunami Golden Gate Bridge boat scene
what_happens: As a tsunami rolls into San Francisco Bay, Ray and Emma power a small boat straight up the face of the wave while a container ship is swept over and smashes into the Golden Gate Bridge.
why: The climb up the wall of water is framed from the boat's bow and from wide aerials, so the tiny craft and the giant ship read clearly against the bridge; pure, cleanly composed digital disaster spectacle.

scene: The glowing whale
query: Life of Pi whale bioluminescent scene
what_happens: On a calm night the ocean around Pi's lifeboat lights up with glowing jellyfish, and a huge whale breaches through the bioluminescence, scattering his raft and supplies into the sea.
why: Ang Lee and Rhythm & Hues design the night as a painting in light, using stereoscopic depth, mirror-like water and a slow reveal so the moment plays as wonder and danger at once.

scene: Wingsuit jump into Chicago
query: Transformers Dark of the Moon wingsuit scene Chicago
what_happens: Soldiers leap from aircraft in wingsuits and swoop between Chicago's skyscrapers, threading through the Decepticon-occupied city to slip past the alien defences.
why: Bay filmed real wingsuit flyers soaring past the city's towers and combined their footage with CG robots, giving the sequence a physical sense of speed and vertigo rare in the franchise.

scene: Flight 1549 ditches in the Hudson
query: Sully Hudson landing scene
what_happens: Seconds after a bird strike kills both engines, Sully glides the airliner over Manhattan and sets it down on the Hudson; passengers spill onto the wings and ferries race to pull them from the icy water.
why: Eastwood shot almost the whole film with IMAX cameras and replays the landing from cockpit, cabin and river, so the pilots' procedural calm contrasts with passenger panic, building suspense from an outcome everyone knows.
period: Hudson River, New York City, 15 January 2009

scene: The blowout
query: Deepwater Horizon blowout explosion scene
what_happens: Mud and gas surge up the well onto the drill floor, then ignite; explosions rip through the rig at night as workers are thrown across the decks and fight through fire toward the lifeboats.
why: Berg built a huge practical rig set and set it ablaze, so the actors react to real heat and fire; the build from mud spray to fireball is cut with procedural detail that makes the failure comprehensible.
period: Deepwater Horizon rig, Gulf of Mexico, 20 April 2010

scene: The tsunami opening
query: Hereafter tsunami scene
what_happens: A French journalist shopping in a Thai beach town is caught by the 2004 tsunami and swept underwater through streets choked with cars and debris until she is pulled out, lifeless, and revived.
why: Eastwood's rare effects set-piece combines tank-shot underwater submersion with seamless digital wave work, staying tight on one woman's disorientation so a global disaster is lived as a single near-death.

scene: The collision — Melancholia strikes the Earth
query: Melancholia ending scene planet collision
what_happens: Justine, her sister Claire and young Leo sit holding hands inside a frame of branches on the lawn as the giant blue planet Melancholia fills the sky and engulfs the Earth.
why: Von Trier holds an almost static wide frame as the planet swells and the wind rises, scoring the end of everything to Wagner; refusing cuts or rescue makes apocalypse feel intimate and serene rather than thrilling.
period: A country estate at the end of the world

scene: The plane crash beside the highway
query: Knowing plane crash scene
what_happens: Stuck in rain-soaked highway traffic, John Koestler watches an airliner plunge into the field beside him and runs into the wreckage, where burning survivors stagger out of the flames.
why: Proyas stages the crash as a single unbroken shot that follows Cage from his car into the inferno, blending a digital aircraft with practical fire and stunt performers so the disaster unfolds without the relief of a cut.

scene: Route 23 log-truck pile-up
query: Final Destination 2 log truck highway scene
what_happens: On a busy highway, the chains snap on a logging truck and its logs tumble across the lanes, setting off a chain of crashes, impalements and explosions that Kimberly sees in a premonition.
why: Director David R. Ellis, a veteran stunt coordinator, builds the pile-up from small warning details and then delivers real vehicle stunts, practical log rigs and fiery wrecks, making it one of horror's most imitated highway sequences.

scene: The train crash
query: Super 8 train crash scene
what_happens: While a group of kids film their zombie movie at a station at night, a pickup drives head-on into an oncoming Air Force freight train, derailing it in a cascade of flying cars and explosions.
why: Abrams lets the derailment escalate for an absurdly long time, carriages cartwheeling past the fleeing children as their abandoned Super 8 camera keeps rolling, a self-aware homage to Spielberg spectacle.

scene: Evacuation of Manhattan — the bridges fall
query: I Am Legend evacuation scene Manhattan quarantine
what_happens: As the military seals Manhattan, Neville fights through panicked crowds to put his wife and daughter on an evacuation helicopter, then watches it collide with another in mid-air as jets destroy the bridges.
why: Lawrence stages the flashback as a nightmare of crowds, searchlights and soldiers on real Manhattan streets, then makes the helicopter collision a sudden shock that explains Neville's isolation without exposition.

scene: The train-crash nightmare
query: Hugo train crash dream scene
what_happens: Hugo dreams he is on the tracks of the Paris station as a locomotive thunders in, smashes through the buffers and bursts out through the station's great window onto the street below.
why: Scorsese recreates the famous 1895 Montparnasse derailment photograph with a detailed miniature locomotive and set, and stages it in 3D so the dream doubles as a love letter to early cinema's train-arrival thrills.
period: Gare Montparnasse, Paris, 1931, in a dream

scene: Drogon burns King's Landing (S8E5 'The Bells')
query: Game of Thrones The Bells Daenerys burns King's Landing scene
what_happens: After the city's bells ring in surrender, Daenerys and Drogon burn King's Landing street by street, as Arya struggles through collapsing buildings, fleeing crowds and rolling fire.
why: Sapochnik moves the spectacle to ground level, following Arya and terrified civilians through practical ash, fire and crowds so the dragon becomes an unseen force of terror and the audience's sympathies invert.

scene: Max escapes Vecna to 'Running Up That Hill' (S4E4 'Dear Billy')
query: Stranger Things Max Running Up That Hill scene
what_happens: Levitating above her stepbrother's grave under Vecna's curse, Max runs through a crumbling nightmare realm as her friends play her favourite Kate Bush song on a Walkman, giving her the strength to break free.
why: Levy cross-cuts the floating body in the cemetery with Max's flight through a hellish mindscape, building cutting and camera speed with the song so music becomes a literal lifeline; it sent a 1985 track back up the charts.

scene: Collapse of the Star Bridge (S1E1 'The Emperor's Peace')
query: Foundation Star Bridge collapse scene
what_happens: Terrorist bombs sever the Star Bridge, the space elevator linking the capital world Trantor to orbit, and the immense tether falls across the planet-city, killing millions as the Emperors watch.
why: Sanders stages the catastrophe from orbit down to street level, conveying planetary scale through the tether's slow fall against tiny onlookers and the Emperors' cold, calculating reaction.
period: Trantor, capital of the Galactic Empire (fictional)

scene: The Judgment Day is sliced in the Panama Canal (S1E5 'Judgment Day')
query: 3 Body Problem Judgment Day ship sliced scene
what_happens: As the cult's ship Judgment Day sails through the Panama Canal, it passes through an invisible web of nanofibres strung across the channel and is silently sliced into layers, along with everyone aboard.
why: The horror comes from restraint: no explosions, just calm daylight, a slow glide and steel and bodies parting in clean planes, with sound stripped to creaks and slides so the audience absorbs the atrocity in real time.
director: Created by David Benioff, D. B. Weiss and Alexander Woo

scene: Plane-crash aftermath on the beach (S1E1 'Pilot')
query: Lost pilot plane crash beach scene
what_happens: Jack wakes in the jungle and runs onto a beach strewn with the burning wreckage of Oceanic 815, pulling survivors free as a man is sucked into a still-running jet engine that then explodes.
why: Abrams shoots the chaos on a real beach around a real airliner fuselage, moving the handheld camera with Jack from victim to victim so the audience meets the ensemble in one panicked tour of the crash site.
accolades: Emmy: Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series
period: Beach on a mysterious Pacific island, September 2004
